In a final twist, Olwen, who was living out the last few days of her pre-determined lifespan as a replicant, discovers she has been transformed into a Nexus-1 herself and can now live the longer life she wished for. Meanwhile, Cora learns that Helena (Sheila Atim), the woman who raised her and Elias (Lewis Gribben), was a replicant, forcing her to reconsider everything she previously believed about humanity and explore the possibility that humans and replicants aren’t so different after all.

Elias, on the other hand, a more radical approach. Determined to fight back against the replicants and reclaim societal control as humans, he broadcasts a message to the population of Los Angeles falsely claiming responsibility for destroying the replicant birthing center in hopes of sparking a human uprising (Julius was the one responsible). But there is no rebellion. The replicants are still in control, and Elias’ fate is unknown.

articles.title: Gerald R. Molen, Oscar-Winning ‘Schindler’s List’ Producer, Dies at 91
articles.summary: Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer behind Steven Spielberg’s “Schindler’s List,” has died. He was 91. Molen’s death was announced by his great-niece, Rachel Lorraine Pullan, in an Instagram post on Sunday. “This morning my great-uncle, Gerald R.
body: Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer behind Steven Spielberg ’s “Schindler’s List,” has died. He was 91.

Molen frequently collaborated with Spielberg throughout his career. He served as producer on “Jurassic Park,” “Minority Report,” “Hook” and “The Lost World: Jurassic Park,” as well as “Schindler’s List,” which won best picture in 1994. Molen shared the Oscar with Spielberg and Branko Lustig. Molen also worked on several Amblin Entertainment films, such as “The Flintstones,” “The Little Rascals,” “Little Giants,” “Casper” and “Twister.”

Molen’s working relationship with Spielberg began in 1985 when he worked as a unit production manager on “The Color Purple.” That job led to an associate producer role on 1987’s “*batteries not included,” on which Spielberg served as executive producer.
Molen’s other producer credits include “Rain Man,” “Days of Thunder,” “Just Like Heaven,” “The Meg,” “Meg 2” and “The Best Christmas Pageant Ever.”

articles.title: Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki Remembered by Singer K.S. Chithra and Suhasini Maniratnam at IFFI’s Lata Mangeshkar Talk
articles.summary: Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki, two of Indian cinema’s most celebrated playback singers, were remembered at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa by singer K.S. Chithra and actor-filmmaker Suhasini Maniratnam.
body: Chithra, who has recorded more than 25,000 songs in several Indian languages over a career spanning nearly five decades, spoke about the singers who shaped her musical sensibilities, among them Mangeshkar, P. Susheela and Janaki. She imitated Janaki as a child, while acknowledging that the veteran singer’s distinctive style was impossible to reproduce. Mangeshkar’s devotional songs, she said, had particularly impressed her with their emotional depth.

Suhasini recalled an episode from the making of “Iruvar” (1997), directed by her husband Mani Ratnam. Composer A.R. Rahman, an Oscar winner for “Slumdog Millionaire,” had invited Bhosle to record a song that needed to evoke the style of Tamil playback singer L.R. Eswari, but was unsure how to explain the reference to her. He asked Suhasini to help. She demonstrated Eswari’s style, and Bhosle went on to deliver “Venilla Venilla.”

Chithra spoke about Bhosle’s versatility and her ability to move between musical forms, including ghazals, and about her desire to establish her own musical identity rather than be compared with her sister. At their first meeting, Chithra said, Bhosle asked her why she was singing in such a high register.

articles.title: You Can See Everything overtly riffs on Vertigo. But how big is its debt to Kiarostami’s Close-Up?
articles.summary: The Iranian film-maker’s 1990 tale of impersonation and deception happens to be a favourite movie of the Elizabeth Holmes docufiction’s co-director Lance Oppenheim • NB: This article contains spoilers.
body: You’re probably sick of hearing how You Can See Everything, about the disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, is the buzziest, coolest, 100% freshest film of the year, but coming out of the screening last week, I couldn’t help but wonder whether Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim had been watching a lot of 90s Iranian cinema. And one film in particular: Close-Up, by Abbas Kiarostami.

If it feels as if You Can See Everything blends truth, lies, fiction and documentary in mind-bending new ways until you’re no longer sure what the hell you’re watching, then Kiarostami, who died in 2016, practically invented this mode 36 years ago. The context could not be more different – analogue 90s Tehran rather than tech-drunk 2020s California – but the themes are the same: Close-Up is a strange story of impersonation, deception and performance, made even stranger by the film-maker’s deliberate meddling.

articles.summary: Arnould first accused Depardieu ⁠in 2018, saying assaults occurred at his Paris home on two separate occasions when ⁠she was in her early 20s. Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping a female actor at his Paris home in 2018, after an appeals ⁠court rejected his…
body: The film star, 77, had appealed last year against an investigating magistrate’s ruling that he should stand criminal trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting Charlotte Arnould on two occasions, but judges said on Thursday proceedings should go ahead.

The court said the star would be tried for allegedly raping Arnould on 7 August 2018, but dismissed a second allegation of rape said to have occurred the following week, on 13 August. Depardieu, one of the best-known names in French cinema, has denied wrongdoing.

Arnould, then 22, first accused Depardieu, whom she had known since childhood, in 2018, ⁠saying the assaults had occurred when she went to the actor’s Parisian townhouse to informally rehearse a play.

The initial indictment, partly upheld on Thursday, ruled that Depardieu should be tried for rape committed through “moral coercion, resulting from a state of shock that prevented Charlotte Arnould from protesting and fleeing”.

articles.title: Huw Edwards gives first interviews since child abuse image conviction
articles.summary: Minister Anna Turley said she was "deeply uncomfortable" with the interviews, while Channel 4 has insisted it "holds Edwards to account".
body: Disgraced former BBC News presenter Huw Edwards has given his first interviews since being convicted in 2024 for making indecent images of children.
Edwards is seen saying he believes "silence is toxic" in a clip of a podcast released by the Observer newspaper, and he has also been interviewed for a Channel 4 documentary.
Government minister Anna Turley told LBC, external she was "deeply uncomfortable" with the interviews, while shadow culture secretary Rebecca Paul said: "This man shouldn't get a minute of airtime".

Channel 4 has defended the documentary. A spokesperson told the BBC that a "highly experienced director" holds Edwards to account with "no questions off limits, revealing his account of what led to his offending and very public downfall".

articles.summary: Actor who had played fraudster Elizabeth Holmes in TV drama The Dropout reveals how she was drafted in to the hit documentary ‘at the last minute’ Amanda Seyfried says that the script and footage of You Can See Everything was kept secret even from her until the last possible moment, and that…
body: Seyfried was speaking on the Jimmy Fallon Show on Tuesday, after the film’s extraordinary commercial success in North America, where it is already the third most successful documentary in box office history. Having already played You Can See Everything’s central figure, Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes, in the dramatised TV series The Dropout, Seyfried was called in by directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim to stand in for Holmes after the latter started her prison term in 2023.

Seyfried said that, after being introduced by fellow actor Emma Stone, Fielder “just reached out and said, ‘Hey, I’d love to, like, pick your brain about, you know, your experience playing Elizabeth Holmes in The Dropout … We talked for like an hour on FaceTime about Elizabeth Holmes, and he told me that he had lived with her for a month before she went to prison.”

“Our undying gratitude also, to our extraordinary team who bravely fought and continue to fight for so hard for what is right and true. On this day, as we all acknowledge the blessings in our lives, we send our love and eternal gratitude to each and every one of you,” Gilbert added, who has been married to Busfield since 2013. articles.title: Protesters disrupt Sir Paul Smith's book talk
articles.summary: The fashion firm says it is committed to animal welfare following protests at a book tour event.
body: Fashion firm Paul Smith has told the BBC it is committed to animal welfare after protesters disrupted a talk by the brand's founder in his home city.
Two supporters of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) interrupted the event hosted by Sir Paul Smith at Nottingham's Broadway Cinema on Wednesday.
The protest follows investigations by PETA into alleged animal cruelty at mohair production facilities in South Africa and Lesotho, including one it said had links to a Paul Smith supplier.
The company said it upheld the highest standards of animal welfare across its supply chain.
